fields.before: A robust Arctic balaenid with a high arched head, white chin, broad flukes and no dorsal fin or right-whale callosity pattern. Individuals accumulate scars and vary in chin-patch extent.
fields.after: A rotund Arctic baleen whale with an enormous bow-shaped head, high lower lips, a white chin, short broad flippers and wide horizontal flukes. Like right whales, it has no dorsal fin and feeds with long baleen. It lacks the right whales' characteristic head callosities.

after.name: Arched rostrum, high lips and white chin
after.description: The upper head is strongly arched and the large head is approximately one-third of body length. Tall lower lips enclose the long baleen. The selected adult has an irregular white anterior lower jaw interrupted by small dark islands; chin extent, grey sloughing and scars vary among individuals. Bowheads have smooth skin without the characteristic right-whale callosity fields.

after.name: Two long baleen racks and oral anatomy
after.description: Two rows of narrow, flexible keratin plates descend from the upper jaw; their lingual edges carry fine fringes. Plates are shorter at the front and rear and longer in the middle. About 320 plates per side are drawn for this reconstruction, within the roughly 300–330 count described in sources. A dark palate, deep oral floor and bulky tongue accompany the moving lower jaw. Select Skim-feeding posture to expose them. The geometry illustrates arrangement; dimensions, fringe density, flexibility, food transport and cross-flow are not measured or solved.

after.name: Finless body, broad flukes and Arctic physiology
after.description: A stocky body has no dorsal fin or rorqual throat pleats. Short broad flippers and a broad, notched horizontal tail complement dorsoventral posterior strokes. Paired elevated blowholes are represented on the head. Thick blubber provides insulation and energy storage; a palatal vascular organ has been proposed to dissipate heat. The exterior does not reveal a measured blubber layer or simulate circulation, gas exchange, oxygen use or heat transfer.

The anterior body stays fixed, with selected posterior bending and slight pectoral articulation on the same skin, pigment and topology, then neutral hold. The study is not a full swimming trajectory, measured speed, universal stroke rate, hydrodynamic solution or physiological validation.
